kiln_p02_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_001.text: The clinic occupied a house behind the grain market, where patients entered beside a woman selling steamed roots. Yue bought breakfast before going in. The examiner had already received her earlier fourth-stage record through the kiln's ordinary appointment book. She read it with the same attention she gave Yue's account of sleeping badly on the road. A previous pass could tell her where to begin; it could not tell her how much work Yue could tolerate today. She asked first about sensation, appetite and the weight of the pack.

kiln_p02_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_002.text: Yue admitted that she had carried the pack farther than necessary on the last travel day. Her shoulders had recovered after a full night, and ordinary touch felt equal on both sides. The examiner checked that statement before opening the reference case. She made Yue distinguish a warm metal lead from an uncharged one while looking away. Yue missed the first comparison because somebody outside dropped a tray. They repeated after the noise passed. The examiner wrote the interruption beside the result instead of pretending that calm had been continuous.

kiln_p02_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_003.text: The reserve reading was modest: nineteen usable breath-units after the appointment's sampling loss, with compatibility a little above eighty-eight percent. Yue felt foolishly disappointed. Her old best had been higher. The examiner asked whether that old best had followed travel, unfamiliar food and a new bed. It had not. A quiet baseline earned under today's conditions was more useful than a number borrowed from an easier morning. Yue watched the woman enter both figures without choosing the more flattering one. The ink made disappointment look smaller and more practical.

kiln_p02_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_004.text: They tested the two established arm pairs separately, resting and discharging between the permitted small tasks. Yue interrupted the second task when called, although the unfinished copper thread annoyed her. The examiner changed the order on a later demonstration and checked the release again. No leg route was attempted. Today's check supported ordinary fourth-stage practice within the recovered limit, pending the following morning's sensation review. It was not another stage examination. Yue took the result back to the kiln as though carrying a bowl she had not yet learned to fill.

kiln_p02_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_005.text: Peng read the work limits before reading the successful comparisons. She moved Yue's first lifting assignment to two people and gave the recovered morning check a place in the roster. Yue almost protested that she had lifted heavier loads elsewhere. Then she saw Luo's broad back passing the door beneath a stack of empty frames. Even his ordinary strength did not make a narrow passage wider. She accepted the changed task. Peng looked pleased without congratulating her, which somehow made acceptance easier. On the wage slate, the shift still counted as work.

kiln_p02_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_006.text: The clay inquiry began with three empty bowls, a sieve and a jar of clean water. Han fetched them from the ordinary testing shelf. He set the bowls in a row and asked Yue which looked least likely to fall. All three had warped bases. They wedged them with folded cloth before starting, and Zhu declared that the academy of broken bowls had accepted a new student. Yue weighed the first dry sample twice. The room was cold enough that Han held his hands beneath his armpits between measurements.

kiln_p02_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_007.text: Neither a red grain nor a patched sack proved deliberate substitution. Luo said this before anybody touched the first sample. White clay could contain iron-bearing flecks; reclaimed clay could have been carefully sorted; an honest bag could split on an honest journey. He wanted ordinary evidence before selecting a kiln programme. They took small recorded samples from the disputed bin and from the separate reclaim stock. The main lots remained closed. Yue liked the feeling of a question becoming three things that could sit on a table instead of one accusation.

kiln_p02_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_008.text: Zhu showed her how to wet a pinch without drowning the texture. Yue rubbed too hard and made every sample feel fine. Zhu stopped her wrist with the handle of a brush, then demonstrated on her own palm. Small hard pieces remained when she used the lighter pressure. Some were sand; some had the sharp curve of previously fired clay. The difference could be checked under a simple lens, not merely believed because a skilled worker had felt it. Yue rinsed her fingers and began again, less eager to seem naturally good at clay.

kiln_p02_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_009.text: Han made tiny bars from each sample and marked them before drying. One bar sagged as he lifted it from the board. He laughed and placed it among the practice failures, where a sag still had something to teach. The disputed sample needed more water to become workable than the ordinary fresh reference. That alone did not establish its source. They recorded the difference and kept the drying bars separate. Yue asked how long they would wait. Until the bar was ready, Han answered. Asking angrily did not make the water leave faster.

kiln_p02_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_010.text: Tan appeared with a new copy of the purchaser's letter and a cup of tea gone almost black. The instruction allowed prepared body for ordinary storage vessels but specified retained fresh material for the small teaching sample. He had previously treated the shared trade name as sufficient. Now he stood beside the bins with the letter folded along that sentence. Luo asked when he had received the page. Tan said three days before Yue arrived. A clerk could make an honest mistake. Receiving a page late did not explain failing to read it.

kiln_p02_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_011.text: Tan's ears reddened when Peng asked for the original receiving date rather than a new clean copy. He fetched the outer letter from his drawer. Its edge had been used to flatten a stain on the tea shelf. Yue saw a corner of the missing sentence darkened by the wet mark, though the words themselves remained readable. She wished the damage had been dramatic enough to explain everything. Instead it was ordinary carelessness, the kind she understood. Peng kept the damaged original and let the clean copy travel with the inquiry.

kiln_p02_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_012.text: The afternoon's ordinary work did not stop because the inquiry was interesting. Shelves still needed sweeping, cold pieces needed sorting and the kiln's children came to reclaim a hoop left beneath a cart. Yue returned the hoop before somebody moved the cart over it. Its owner solemnly explained that one spoke was better than the others for jumping. Zhu asked whether that advantage had been independently tested. The child said yes, by herself, which was the person who mattered. Yue laughed so hard that she nearly dropped the empty sorting basket.

kiln_p02_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_013.text: At the shift's end, Jian waited outside the archive with his tablet wrapped in an old scarf. The river witness had not returned. Peng's promised interim answer said that the claim remained open, the wage portion was already paid, and study credit for schedule marking depended on the witness and the learning agreement. Jian read it in silence. Yue expected him to shout. Instead he asked whether an open claim could still become a refused one. Peng said yes. Then he asked whether refusing it would explain why. She answered yes to that too.

kiln_p02_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_014.text: Jian wanted the entire night recognised as apprenticeship. Peng could not promise that hauling empty frames had taught the skill his agreement named. She could promise that the schedule task would be judged on what he had done, including any instruction he had received. He stared at the line describing supervised work. "If nobody bothered to watch, do I become somebody who learned nothing?" he asked. The room went quiet. Peng set the pen down. Absence of a required supervisor might be the institution's failure even when it prevented certification of a particular skill.

kiln_p02_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_015.text: Yue had spent much of her life wanting the next lesson to be available. Jian was already inside a workshop and could still be shut out by the shape of an entry. She asked whether he had kept the actual cooling marks he made. He had kept a practice copy, with his mistakes crossed through. Peng asked to inspect it with his permission. The boy looked embarrassed by the errors. Yue showed him the crooked little stand in her own task basket. Zhu had nicknamed it the Foreman's Throne. Jian's mouth moved despite himself.

kiln_p02_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_016.text: His practice schedule mixed two cooling programmes, one for thick storage jars and one for thin cups. The mistakes were useful because somebody had corrected them in a different hand. Luo recognised his own blunt numerals. He had instructed Jian for part of that night, then forgotten the separate credit line while answering a late delivery. The witness could still establish the duration and what Jian completed afterward. Luo said this in front of Peng and Jian. His admission did not solve the whole claim. It removed one reason the boy had been forced to argue alone.

kiln_p02_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_017.text: Luo offered to begin a fresh supervised schedule exercise the following week, outside the hours already disputed. Jian flared at the suggestion. A new exercise would not pay back the old one. Luo agreed. He was offering a way to keep learning while the old claim was decided, and the new record would identify the teacher before work began. Yue watched Jian struggle with an answer he clearly wanted to refuse. Finally he said he would attend, but he wanted the old tablet kept. Peng placed it in a labelled cover rather than rubbing anything away.

kiln_p02_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_018.text: The next morning's clinic review found no new numbness, tremor or pain after Yue's small tests. The examiner asked her to grip an ordinary wooden handle and stand from the bench without preparation. Those simple movements felt stranger than the copper task because Yue knew exactly how easy they ought to be. They were easy. Permission for limited established-route maintenance continued. The examiner advised returning after a fortnight of settled work before discussing new training. Yue had hoped to begin sooner. She ate a second steamed root on the way out and let hope wait.

kiln_p02_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_019.text: A runner brought word that the river store had closed its cart road after a bank slip. The missing witness would arrive by the longer footpath, probably the following day. The same closure delayed the retained clay sample Tan had requested. Luo refused to turn the delay into a guess. He moved the planned small sample firing by two mornings and told the purchaser why. Tan winced at the delivery penalty. Peng asked for the actual clause. There was none for that preliminary sample. The penalty had belonged to a different order Tan was trying to finish.

kiln_p02_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_020.text: That other order was for plain water jars, already made and waiting for a sound firing interval. It would pay part of the workshop's winter expenses. Yue could understand why Tan had seen every empty hour as a threat. The understanding did not make the thin cups ready to share a schedule with thick jars. Luo laid both plans side by side and asked which heat change each body had survived in earlier trials. Tan had only a purchaser's assurance for the teaching cups. He folded that assurance smaller while the others looked at the trial shelf.

kiln_p02_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_021.text: On the cold floor, Luo arranged empty props to show why a full shelf was not simply a collection of separate promises. A thick jar shaded one side of a thin cup. A crowded rim changed the air path. The ordinary charcoal flame would find the gaps they actually left, not the tidy spaces in Tan's drawing. Yue moved a prop half a hand and watched the shadow change. She had studied current in careful channels; a kiln asked the same respect from hot moving air. Its paths were larger, dirtier and harder to correct once the door closed.

kiln_p02_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_022.text: Zhu placed one of her deliberately ugly teaching cups between the jar props. Its wide foot occupied more space than the drawing allowed. Tan suggested making the foot narrower. Zhu asked whether he wanted a cup that stood up or a drawing that did. He smiled unwillingly, then said the purchaser's price allowed very little extra shelf space. The joke ended there. Cheap space could become a material instruction even when nobody called it one. Yue copied the actual cup dimensions beside the proposed arrangement and left the purchaser's prettier drawing attached behind them.

kiln_p02_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_023.text: Peng found the original estimate in a packet tied with green thread. It priced ordinary storage ware, with a separate provisional line for four hundred teaching cups if the retained sample passed. The later order had carried the same unit figure into both lines. Nobody had priced the additional inspection and trial fuel. Tan said the association had expected their existing kiln to cover it. Luo said existing equipment still needed charcoal. They counted the trial reserve before arguing about the larger batch. There was enough for two small tests, not for four hundred acts of optimism.

kiln_p02_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_024.text: The charcoal cage smelled sweet and dusty. Yue stood back while Luo opened it for the keeper's count. Large sound pieces lay above a layer of crumbs. The owner had paid for weight; the firing plan needed pieces that would burn at a controllable rate. They did not throw the crumbs away. Ordinary drying heat could use some of them separately. Han fetched a screen and discovered that sorting fuel was much less noble than discussing it. Black dust crept into every wrinkle of Yue's hands. By supper she had earned a worker's complaint about clean towels.

kiln_p02_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_025.text: The screen left them with a smaller usable stock for the promised trial schedule. Luo adjusted the count on the fuel slate and ordered more ordinary charcoal before accepting any larger firing. Tan asked whether the owner would call the discarded portion waste. Nothing had been discarded, Luo said; they had named what each portion could actually do. Yue thought of her nineteen useful breath-units and smiled into the dust. A sack could be full in the wrong way. So could a practitioner. Han saw her smile and accused the charcoal of telling better jokes than he did.

kiln_p02_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_026.text: That evening Zhu took her to the town's bathhouse, where the warmest bench had a leg repaired with a brick. They waited for two old women to finish comparing prices before undressing. Zhu unwrapped the support on her right hand without drama. The wrist looked ordinary until she tried to bend it far backward. Yue looked away too quickly and was caught doing it. "You may see a hand," Zhu said. "It is allowed to be here." Yue apologised for making the injury into a spectacle. Zhu splashed her with perfectly ordinary bathwater.

kiln_p02_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_027.text: In the steam, Zhu described the first month after the loading-door injury. She had hated having work brought to her bed because it meant everyone expected her to remain there. Later she had hated the expectation that recovery meant doing everything exactly as before. Trimming with her left hand had begun as stubbornness and become a real skill, though it did not erase the right hand's limit. Yue listened without offering a cultivation solution. Warm water softened the day's charcoal in their fingernails. It did nothing miraculous to old connective tissue.

kiln_p02_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_028.text: Zhu asked what Yue most wanted from the next stage. Yue said more reliable work through more routes, which sounded like a lesson answer even to her. After a while she admitted wanting not to be the smallest useful person at every accident. Zhu looked at her for a long time. "At our last accident, the smallest useful person rang the right bell," she said. "The largest useful person held a door that should already have been propped." Yue laughed, then stopped. They had both spoken about a kind of helplessness whose shape rank alone would not settle.

kiln_p02_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_029.text: The river witness returned next afternoon with a muddy cloak and a basket of onions she had bought on the long road. She remembered the disputed night because Jian had corrected her count of empty props. She had watched Luo show him the cooling marks, then watched him finish a revised schedule before the late cart arrived. She could not remember an exact hour. Peng did not offer one for her to adopt. The woman drew the sequence of tasks on scrap paper. The onions rolled beneath the table while she was concentrating.

kiln_p02_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_030.text: Jian retrieved the onions so carefully that Yue realised he feared annoying his own witness. The woman thanked him and asked why everyone looked ready for a funeral. Peng explained the credit dispute in plain terms. The witness said Jian had worked hard, but she would not pretend to have watched every moment of it. That qualification hurt him. It also made the part she did remember harder to dismiss. Luo confirmed the instruction she described. Tan, called from the order room, listened with his hands inside his sleeves and no tea cup to hold.

kiln_p02_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_031.text: Peng accepted credit for the supervised schedule exercise, identifying the portion supported by Luo, the corrected practice copy and the witness. Ordinary moving and cleaning remained paid labor. The missing supervision on a later task became a workshop action, not a fault placed on Jian. The award was smaller than the whole night he had claimed. He read it twice and asked whether the explanation could accompany the number. Peng fastened both pages into his tablet cover. Yue saw his shoulders loosen a little. A smaller true entry had become something that could travel without his anger carrying it.

kiln_p02_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_032.text: Tan said he had promised that preparation would count because he had expected Luo to sign the entire night. Luo replied that expectation had become an instruction in the boy's ears. They needed to agree what a task meant before using his fatigue. Nobody shouted. The quiet was worse for Tan. He offered to amend future assignments himself. Peng accepted the work but kept the review of the missed supervision with the keeper. Jian did not thank him. He took the tablet outside, where Han was trying to persuade the sorting basket to hold one more cracked bowl.

kiln_p02_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_033.text: Yue found Jian by the cold kiln door after work. He asked whether she thought he should be grateful. She said she thought he was allowed to feel several things at once. He admitted that the new exercise frightened him. If he performed badly under supervision, people might decide he had never deserved the old credit. Yue remembered the low reserve reading and told him about it. He seemed relieved that a fourth-stage practitioner could be disappointed by an ordinary number. They compared their embarrassments until the cold drove them both toward supper.

kiln_p02_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_034.text: The next retained clay sample arrived in a covered pot accompanied by a river-store receiving slip. Its original lot number matched the first fresh invoice. Its body felt different from the disputed bin under Zhu's light touch. They made new ordinary test bars and left them beside the earlier ones, still waiting for sufficient drying. Tan read the slip while Luo inspected the seal. The pot had remained at the river store after the first cart was redirected. Yue asked where that cart had gone. Tan answered, "Back to preparation," then seemed to hear how little that explained.

kiln_p02_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_035.text: On the following workday, Peng authorised a visit to the town depot with Tan, Yue and the store keeper. The inquiry concerned paid material, not a search of somebody's home. The depot clerk welcomed them until he saw both invoices. Then he took the papers into an inner room and kept them there long enough for Yue to count the pigeons beneath the rafters. Four birds settled on a sack marked for fine white clay. One pecked at a torn corner and spat out a crumb. Han would have enjoyed the animal's review.

kiln_p02_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_036.text: The depot's owner emerged carrying a board still wet from washing. On it lay three delivery tokens, each with a stamped number. The first fresh lot had been returned when the purchaser asked for a prepared body suitable for cheaper storage vessels. The depot had treated that change as an exchange, weighing the returned clay into its stock and issuing prepared material at the old weight. Its exchange note should have accompanied the second invoice. Tan asked for the note. The owner produced a carbon copy with the lower half folded behind a receipt.

kiln_p02_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_037.text: The note credited the lower material price, but its destination was a balance account rather than the kiln's current purse. Tan recognised the account before Peng could ask about it. An older advance to the workshop had remained unpaid. The association had instructed the depot to set any credit against that balance. Two purchases could therefore appear paid in full while the saving vanished into an older debt. Yue could see how the papers had produced one bin. She still could not see who had agreed to use that bin for teaching vessels.

kiln_p02_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_038.text: Tan said the exchange request had arrived while he was arranging the water-jar order. He had read storage vessel and assumed it covered both lines. The depot owner objected that he supplied bodies according to written instructions, not according to the kiln's future lessons. Peng asked to see the request. It named ordinary storage ware and contained no permission to replace the retained teaching material. The error had passed through several ordinary hands. It had not become harmless by belonging to all of them. They copied each document with its date and destination intact.

kiln_p02_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_039.text: The keeper asked for the original retained fresh stock. Most remained in a locked corner awaiting the purchaser's revised direction. A sack opened for sampling had been sewn closed again. Yue examined the seam and thought of the patched bag at the gate, but she did not equate them. The depot owner explained that he used the same stitch on every opened sack. Its familiarity would make a poor identifier. They checked the numbered receiving board instead. The original stock could be restored for a fresh price difference that the kiln had not budgeted.

kiln_p02_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_040.text: Peng requested a written account before choosing whether to reverse the exchange. The depot owner wanted their signatures immediately because the pigeons had begun fighting over a spilled handful of grain. Tan stepped forward to sign. Peng caught the edge of the board rather than his hand. They were acknowledging receipt of the explanation, she said, not accepting the proposed settlement. The owner looked offended until she showed him the exact line. He crossed out the word settled and wrote received. Outside, the pigeons settled their own dispute by flying to another roof.

kiln_p02_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_041.text: The party returned along the market lane, where a mule had backed a vegetable cart into a shallow ditch. Its driver was pulling the reins harder with every unsuccessful attempt. Yue stopped beside the ditch and asked him to let the animal breathe. The cart's right wheel was caught behind a stone. Tan looked irritated by the delay until the keeper handed him two empty baskets to unload. They lightened the cart, propped the axle and called a nearby porter. Ordinary hands freed the wheel while the mule stood chewing a stolen cabbage leaf.

kiln_p02_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_042.text: Tan laughed at the cabbage thief, his first easy laugh of the day. Then he remembered the papers and became careful again. Yue wondered how much effort he spent arranging his face for different rooms. He offered to carry the empty baskets back to their owner. The offer was unnecessary and useful; she let him do it. They reached the kiln with cold fingers and no heroic story. Peng had paid the porter from the driver's offered coins, not from the material inquiry. Each small part of the rescue belonged to the person who had actually supplied it.

kiln_p02_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_043.text: Luo read the depot account while standing, then sat down before reaching the older advance. He remembered that advance as wages kept moving during last winter's roof repair. Tan remembered it as a line that never stopped attracting new conditions. Neither recollection changed the current material instruction. They could use the prepared body for an ordinary storage trial if its physical tests passed. They could not use the same result to certify charged teaching cups. Luo separated those programmes on the slate. The space between them looked wider than the price difference had looked on paper.

kiln_p02_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_044.text: The purchaser's local agent came at dusk wearing boots too clean for the yard. He asked why the sample had not fired. Peng showed him the retained-material sentence before showing the exchange note. He said the association had assumed the kiln would understand the economical alternative. Zhu asked whether his assumption could hold a hot cup after an imperfect discharge. He did not answer the question. Instead he praised the workshop's resourcefulness. Yue had heard that praise before, usually when somebody wanted the cost of a problem moved into the hands solving it.

kiln_p02_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_045.text: Luo asked the agent to take two concrete proposals back: pay to restore fresh material and fund its separate trial, or keep the order limited to ordinary storage ware. The agent said a larger teaching commission might be lost if the association received an uncertain answer. Luo turned one of the cold cracked cups so its hidden body line faced the lamp. An uncertain answer was precisely what they presently had. The agent looked at the line and stopped talking about larger orders. He took both proposals, leaving no agreement that the trial had passed merely because the discussion ended.

kiln_p02_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_046.text: Zhu wanted to throw something after he left. Han offered the sagging practice bar, then rescued it when she actually reached for it. They settled for taking turns flicking clay crumbs into the empty reclaim bucket. Yue missed three times. Jian, passing with a clean schedule board, hit the bucket without looking. Zhu accused him of wasting his greatest talent on a respected trade. The boy bowed with exaggerated dignity. Their laughter lasted only a few breaths, but Yue felt the yard become theirs again. Tomorrow's work could begin in a place that had survived tonight's visitor.

kiln_p02_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_047.text: The bars dried slowly in the cold. Luo kept them away from the hottest wall rather than buying speed with a new crack. Yue checked their mass at the agreed intervals and found that one reference lost less water than she expected. Han noticed the bowl beneath it had been weighed with a cloth pad attached. They corrected the comparison and repeated it. Yue wanted to bury the mistaken entry. Han made her leave it legible, with the reason written beside the new result. An archive without ordinary errors would teach newcomers to hide ordinary errors.

kiln_p02_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_048.text: She began to understand why Peng kept failed firings rather than only successful samples. A successful cup could tell them that one arrangement worked once. A failed shelf might show how its makers had misunderstood the air, the body or each other. That afternoon Yue matched the cold tags to their cooling slates. Two slates used the same little hook-shaped mark for different actions. One meant close the outer shutter; the other meant check its position. She copied both on separate cards and asked Luo which his current crew used. He sighed before answering.

kiln_p02_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_049.text: The crew used both. Older workers knew the distinction from the slates' paper colour. The new paper supply had only one colour. Luo had noticed the change but not the consequence. They wrote the action beside the mark for current schedules and kept the old examples for instruction. Jian asked whether his corrected practice copy would count as wrong if he had used the old shorthand. Peng said the answer depended on what he had been taught at the time. Yue could almost feel the boy resisting the temptation to claim another easy injustice before checking.

kiln_p02_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_050.text: His next supervised exercise used a cold mock shelf. Luo asked him to explain which action the mark required before moving any ordinary shutter. Jian answered well on the first arrangement and missed the changed one. He scowled at the paper as though it had betrayed him. Luo waited until he found the missing instruction. Yue watched from her archive task, glad she was not being assessed and ashamed of that gladness. When Jian succeeded on the repeated exercise, nobody awarded a new rank. They recorded the small demonstrated skill he could now use without guessing.

kiln_p02_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_051.text: At lunch, Yue asked Han how long he had worked in clay. He considered the question and said it depended whether years spent making bad clay things counted. His father had expected him to mend baskets. His first bowl sold for less than a good basket because it rocked on the table. Now his bowls stood squarely and his baskets still looked like traps for unfortunate chickens. Yue asked whether he regretted the years. He said he regretted one particular winter, then stole her pickle while she was deciding whether to ask about it.

kiln_p02_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_052.text: That evening she wrote home again. She described the clay inquiry as work in progress and the Foreman's Throne as an object unlikely to find a buyer. She included the ordinary wage rate and the dry bed, knowing those details would matter more than a description of any copper glow. Her mother had worked too many uncertain seasons to trust the sentence I am doing well without a meal behind it. Yue almost described Zhu's hand, then chose to describe her humor instead. A friend was more than the injury that had made her memorable.

kiln_p02_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_053.text: Peng let her make a study copy of one cooling slate after removing the purchaser's private account line. The original remained in the archive. Yue carried the copy upstairs and discovered that her roommate had spread wet socks across the table. They negotiated for a clear corner with the gravity of officials dividing a river. Her roommate offered the warmest chair in compensation. Yue could not see a spiritual route through that ordinary courtesy, but she felt its effect. She spent the evening studying comfortably instead of proving she could tolerate a damp place.

kiln_p02_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_054.text: Late that night, water began dripping behind the lodging stair. At first Yue thought the roof stain had returned. Then a narrow stream spread across the lower landing. She woke the house keeper and moved the shoes out of its path. The pipe beside the outer wall had cracked in the cold. Nobody needed a qi technique to diagnose water running out of a visible split. They closed the household stopcock and fetched buckets. Yue's roommates grumbled, then helped. By the time the flow stopped, every person in the room knew whose shoes leaked.

kiln_p02_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_055.text: The house keeper offered hot tea while they waited for the repairer. Yue felt an impulse to make the waiting useful by practising a little admission. She let it pass. Interrupted sleep and cold feet were conditions to report, not a challenge secretly inserted into her recovered record. Zhu arrived at dawn with an ordinary wrench borrowed from the kiln maintenance cupboard and a warning that she was not the pipe repairer. She helped hold the dry cloth while the hired worker fitted a replacement. The wrench returned before the day shift began.

kiln_p02_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_056.text: Peng altered Yue's morning task after hearing about the broken pipe. Archive work remained possible; heavy loading would wait until her normal sleep recovered. Yue expected somebody to call this favoritism. Instead Han asked whether the new schedule would let her rescue the socks from their damp hostage situation. The kiln paid the agreed shift because the assigned archive task still occupied it. No full night's sleep was entered merely because the day had begun. Yue found the distinction almost comforting. Her body did not need to win an argument against the clock to be believed.

kiln_p02_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_057.text: The ordinary storage bars were ready for a small trial preparation by the week's end. The retained fresh sample needed another drying interval. Luo did not fill the extra space with wet teaching cups. He arranged the dried bars around two plain test vessels whose dimensions were already understood. Yue helped mark the cold positions and learned how to read a witness tile without treating its colour as a universal temperature. The tile matched this firing method and this body. Another kiln's bright shade might mean a different thing. Zhu made her explain that back before signing the setup.

kiln_p02_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_058.text: At the cold setup, Yue reached past a frame to straighten a bar. Luo stopped her before she shifted the frame onto her wrist. She apologised and offered to finish quickly. He told her to come around to the clear side. The safer route took three more steps. She took them with a hot face. Jian watched, then quietly moved his own board away from the same awkward reach. Neither of them turned the correction into a moral victory. The bars simply stayed intact, their wrists stayed unhurt, and the task continued without requiring anyone to be exceptional.

kiln_p02_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_059.text: Tan brought the association's answer on the sixth completed shift of Yue's appointment. They would fund the restored fresh material for the retained sample, but would decide the larger teaching order afterward. The ordinary forty-cup storage commission remained separate. There was no instruction to combine the trial with the jar batch. The answer was narrower than he wanted and clearer than the previous one. Luo accepted the funded sample plan. Peng returned the older credit question to its own account review. A new payment for clay would not quietly erase a dispute about last winter's advance.

kiln_p02_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_060.text: Yue received thirty-six copper for her six completed paid shifts, in addition to the six she had earned on the trial day. She counted the coins in the keeper's room, then folded most into her personal travel purse. The meal and bed provision did not create another deduction. She bought a little fresh ginger for the upstairs pot and declined a bright ribbon displayed beside it. The ribbon was beautiful. She wanted to leave it beautiful on the seller's board rather than turn every wage into proof that hardship had finally ended.

kiln_p02_061.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_061.text: Zhu bought the ribbon after seeing Yue hesitate, then refused to make it a gift. She needed it for a friend's daughter's festival braid and was delighted that somebody else had already tested its attractiveness. Yue accused her of conducting an unauthorised beauty trial. Zhu offered to record the result on a clay bar. They walked back laughing, and the town's low winter sun lit the powder on Zhu's sleeves. Yue remembered how little she had known at the gate. The people inside were becoming difficult to describe only by their work titles.

kiln_p02_062.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_062.text: Jian received a small wage remainder that evening, owed from an ordinary task entered late during the dispute. It was money rather than apprenticeship credit, and he looked almost surprised to be pleased by it. He bought two fried cakes, gave one to Yue and demanded an honest comparison with the bakery near her home. She said this one was better while hot and worse after cooling. He frowned until she explained that it was still hot. They ate beside the cold kiln. No document needed to certify their brief agreement about the cake.

kiln_p02_063.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_063.text: He said his father had wanted him to become a river clerk. An apprentice looked noble from far away, but a clerk could usually keep his hands clean and know when he would be paid. Yue asked whether his father was still waiting for him to change his mind. Jian nodded. His brother's hanging bed was real; the family had moved into a room too narrow for two sleeping mats. Jian made every extra bit of credit into a future doorway. Yue understood the pressure without promising that the next assessment could supply a house.

kiln_p02_064.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_064.text: When the archive closed, Peng took the corrected material papers downstairs. The original exchange request joined the damaged instruction and both invoices in one packet. Yue had made an index rather than a verdict. Peng asked what she thought had happened. She described the substitution the papers established, then the missing link: nobody had shown that prepared storage body was authorised for teaching cups. The keeper nodded and asked who would benefit from accepting that gap. Yue named several people, including the workers spared another trial. Benefit alone would not identify deliberate wrongdoing.

kiln_p02_065.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_065.text: That question followed her upstairs. She herself would benefit from a smooth commission that kept training funded. Luo would benefit from a full useful winter. Tan would benefit from fewer debts, Jian from more supervised hours, the purchaser from cheaper cups. A mistake could travel because everyone wanted a different good thing at its end. Yue wrote that thought in her private study margin, then crossed out the last grand sentence. It sounded wiser than what she had proved. She kept the simpler question: what does this material actually survive?

kiln_p02_066.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_066.text: The next morning, before any trial flame, Han found a thin crack in one of the dried bars. It followed a red particle embedded near the end. Luo kept it as a specimen and removed it from the passing group. The batch did not fail merely because one test piece had failed during drying; neither could that piece be hidden to make the remaining count look prettier. Yue labelled its position and history. Zhu turned it under the lens. The particle had an old glazed surface on one side, confirming at least some fired reclaim in the disputed body.

kiln_p02_067.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_067.text: The prepared supplier had permitted sorted fired reclaim for ordinary ware, so the particle did not itself prove fraud. Its size did raise a practical problem for thin vessels. Luo asked for the preparation screen specification before choosing how much of the remaining body could be used. Tan disliked another request but wrote it anyway. Yue carried the tagged bar into the archive and found an older shelf failure with a similar particle. Its card had been filed under uneven heat. She felt the inquiry begin to widen beyond one recent invoice and one tired clerk.

kiln_p02_068.speaker: narrator
kiln_p02_068.text: Peng would not let her rename the old failure after looking at one fragment. They needed the retained body sample, the original firing slate and the maker's account if any survived. Yue found two of those items and a note that referred to an apprentice whose final credit sheet was missing from the same year. Jian, entering with his new exercise board, saw the empty field and went very still. The clay question had led to another person's learning record. Yue placed a bookmark in the packet. Tomorrow they would begin by finding what the archive still knew.
